idw / Landesamt für Denkmalpflege und Archäologie Sachsen-Anhalt (8 Aug 2023) — publication of the excavation by Norma Henkel (about 150 circular enclosures known from the central and eastern European Middle Neolithic; Stroke-ornamented Pottery culture c. 4900–4600/4550 BC; found by Otto Braasch in 1991; open to the public since 2005; two concentric palisades; three entrances N, SE, SW; SE and SW gaps match winter-solstice sunrise and sunset; other gaps match the summer solstice and 30 April; cattle-skull fragments and about 30 horn cores in the ditch area; pits with burnt remains and human bones)

bild der wissenschaft — 'Kult im Kreislauf der Konstellation' (75 m across; reconstruction of ditch, bank and two palisades in 2005 on the original post holes, Bertemes quote; palisades rebuilt 2.40 m high, originals perhaps nearer 3 m; winter-solstice window fixed to about four days; builders had cosmological knowledge similar to the makers of the Nebra Sky Disc made some 3,000 years later)

Volksstimme — 'Tausende Gäste am Ringheiligtum' (Goseck: 75 m diameter, three gates, double ring of oak palisades about 2 m high with an earth bank; about 25 km from the find site of the Nebra Sky Disc; part of the 'Himmelswege' tourist route)

abu_simbel.label: Wikipedia — Abu Simbel (Great Temple c. 1264–1244 BC, about 20 years' work; facade 33 m high and 38 m wide; four seated colossi about 20 m; frieze of 22 baboons; sanctuary statues of Ra-Horakhty, deified Ramesses, Amun-Ra and Ptah; sunlight on about 22 October and 22 February, Ptah 'a god connected with the realm of the dead' stays dark; birthday/coronation link 'allegedly', no direct evidence; date drift from precession plus relocation; Burckhardt 1813, Belzoni 1 August 1817; 1964–68 rescue: 1,036 blocks (807 Great Temple), raised 65 m and moved 208 m, US$41.7 million shared by Egypt and 48 countries, crowns and 19-tonne faces cut to fit 30-tonne cranes, sunbeam checked on 22 February 1966 at 63.1 m inside, inauguration 22 September 1968; UNESCO 1979)

Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum — New Kingdom Monuments: Abu Simbel (colossi about 21 m; light reaches the inner sanctuary on 22 October and 22 February and lights three seated statues; link with coronation and birth only hypothesised; moved 1964–68 about 64 m higher; because of the move and/or the slow drift of the Tropic of Cancer the events have shifted by about one day)

UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae (inscribed 1979; temples of Ramesses II saved from the rising Nile by the international campaign launched by UNESCO; Great Temple carved out of an escarpment of solid rock, sunlight reaches the innermost chamber twice a year)
Wikipedia — Ramesses II (born c. 1303 BC, ruled c. 1279–1213 BC; accession most often dated to 31 May 1279 BC)
Serbian Wikipedia — Абу Симбел (spelling Abu Simbel, Ramzes II, Nefertari; temples raised 65 m higher; Burkhard found them in 1813)
